subject: Dedicated hardware risk & hedge plan for NovA (SKU tradeoffs and fallthrough)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@novumai.com>, Nicole Zhang <nicole@cloudprovider.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated hardware risk & hedge plan for NovA (SKU tradeoffs and fallthrough)

Team —

Quick background: NovumAI is advancing from our Hosted API pilot to a Dedicated contract (NOVA-2351). Their primary workload mixes long-context generative completions (8k–32k tokens, RLHF ended) and high-volume embedding pipelines. Procurement pushed for a cost-optimized SKU mix but wants firm latency SLOs.

Ask: I need a concise recommendation for a starting SKU allocation (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and a fallback/hedge policy we can commit in the SOW. Key customer constraints:
- 99th percentile completion latency <= 350ms for short queries, <= 1.5s for long context golden path
- Peak concurrent streams: ~180 production sessions, batch embedding jobs (nightly) heavy
- Data residency: US-only, prefer us-west primary

Initial thoughts (from sales):
- H100 for long-context models and memory-bound RLHF artifacts
- A100 for steady-state throughput + tiling-friendly models
- L4 for embeddings and low-cost burst/offload

Please review the attached sizing workbook (NOVA-2351-sizing-workbook.xlsx) and quant summary. We need a recommended split, a fallthrough plan if H100 inventory is constrained, and a short paragraph on cost delta (reserve vs burst) we can feed to procurement.

Target: get back by EOD so I can surface to Samir for Friday procurement meeting.

Thanks —
Karthik
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: NOVA-2351-sizing-workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), quant_summary.pdf (2 pages)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@novumai.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated hardware risk & hedge plan for NovA (SKU tradeoffs and fallthrough)

Karthik —

Thanks for the brief. High-level recommendation from infra/ops perspective (short version):

1) Baseline mix to propose in the SOW (initial 12-month commit):
   - H100 (80GB): 18 slots (~20% of active pool) — reserved for long-context golden-paths and non-tilable models
   - A100 (80GB): 54 slots (~60% of active pool) — primary workhorse for generation throughput and tiled long-context fallbacks
   - L4 (24GB): 18 slots (~20% of active pool) — embedding offload, low-latency lightweight responses, and pre-processing

Rationale: H100s give headroom for large KV caches and sparse-attention optimizations; A100s are much more cost-efficient for steady token throughput when you can tile or quantize; L4s are ideal to push embedding and classifier workloads off the expensive pool.

2) Fallthrough / hedge policy (operational):
   - Capacity shortfall (H100 unavailable): automatically route long-context requests to A100 with enforced tiling + dynamic KV flushing and a conservative max_token cap (configurable per-route).
   - If A100 tail latencies degrade > SLO, degrade non-critical background embedding batches to L4 pool and throttle new session startups (graceful 10% admission-control).
   - Canary rollout: start new model version in H100 subset (5%) then expand to A100 with fallback toggles for quantized kernels.

3) Cost deltas (high-level):
   - H100 reserve price ~ 2.2x A100 per-month for equivalent slot throughput on memory-bound workloads.
   - Offloading embeddings to L4 reduces per-embedding cost by ~60% relative to H100 and ~40% vs A100 (ballpark).

4) Telemetry + guardrails: token-level cost tagging, per-route latency alarms, and a weekly quantitative report to NovumAI during onboarding.

I attached a short ops-runbook (ops-runbook-dedicated.txt) with failover scripts and the suggested autoscale thresholds. Ben, can you confirm GPU availability windows for us-west and whether Reserved + Burst is feasible for this mix?

—Irene
Director, Platform Operations

Attachment: ops-runbook-dedicated.txt (runbook, 6 pages)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@novumai.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated hardware risk & hedge plan for NovA (SKU tradeoffs and fallthrough)

Irene / team —

Quick availability & ops constraints from capacity planning:
- Current us-west pool: A100 (60 slots immediately available), H100 (8 slots available), L4 (25 slots). H100 procurement lead time for additional 12 units is ~9–11 weeks at current vendor cadence.
- Recommendation: make the SOW conservative on guaranteed H100 headcount (commit 18 but plan for conversion to A100 for additional capacity with pre-agreed tiling).
- Headroom: for the SLOs you listed, we recommend auto-scale buffer of +25% reserved concurrency during business hours. That equates to ~22 extra A100-equivalent slots to absorb spikes.

Operational caveats:
- Some of NovumAI's model artifacts appear to be single-file memory heavy; we should include a clause for model-level remediation (quantization/striping) within 30 days to retain H100 pricing.
- If they insist on H100-only fallback, we need an SLA uplift (higher price) or a soft SLA that permits cross-region failover (us-east) during extreme outages.

I've attached a quick CSV with availability snapshots (capacity-availability-us-west.csv). If procurement wants lower cost quickly, we can propose a hybrid start (L4 for embeddings immediately + A100 reserved; H100 ramp to 20% by month 3).

—Ben
Head of Dedicated Ops

Subject: Re: Dedicated hardware risk & hedge plan for NovA (SKU tradeoffs and fallthrough)

Thanks everyone — useful summary. Couple quick items from procurement/technical program manager side:

- Can you send a one-page cost delta table we can use in our procurement review (H100 reserve vs A100 reserve vs mixed with L4 offload)?
- NovumAI wants a 30-day trial option for the proposed mix, with the ability to scale H100 up if model performance shows significant quality degradation. Is a time-boxed trial reasonable?
- For immediate go-live, we want to try L4-first for embeddings (to validate cost savings) and stagger H100 ramp over the first 8 weeks.

If you can get the cost table and a short SOW paragraph about the trial option by EOD Thursday, we can push procurement to sign by next week.

—Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, NovumAI
